content:
elaine_cs: ArborFin is green for prod tomorrow 09:00 PST. They need a temporary regional rate bump in us-west + ap-northeast (JP) and their prod IPs added to the allowlist. They also reported ~300ms p95 from EU which is making their PM nervous — renewal convo next week, want to avoid escalation. Ticket INF-4821 created: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4821. Can infra/network help with routing + a 12hr rate lift and an auto-revoke?
sam_net: Copy. Can you drop the exact IPs and expected QPS/spike profile? Also which routes should be prioritized (region-only or CIDR level)?
elaine_cs: IPs: 52.142.18.4, 3.5.6.200. They have a small proxy pool so we need both. Expected baseline ~200 QPS, spikes up to ~1.2k for ~20-30m after deploy. Prioritize us-west, then ap-northeast, fallback to hosted-eu if capacity constrained.
jin_oncall: We can do a temporary rate window + allowlist. Proposed plan: 
- apply allowlist to customer-prod role for those two IPs
- bump per-customer QPS to 1200 for 12h starting 09:00 PST
- set an automatic revoke at 21:00 PST
Config snippet I will apply:
```
customer_limits: arborfin-prod:
  qps: 1200
  regions: [us-west, ap-northeast]
  auto_revoke: "2026-03-22T21:00:00-08:00"
allowlist: arborfin-prod: [52.142.18.4, 3.5.6.200]
```
sam_net: That looks fine. I'll provision the allowlist on the edge ACL and update the routing policy to steer traffic to us-west/ap-northeast. Will also add a short TTL on the route so we can rollback quickly.
marcus_platform: We can do traffic steering with weighted routing. Suggest weights: us-west 0.85, ap-northeast 0.15 during the spike window, fallback 0 to eu unless both overloaded. I'll add a canary check and a fallback to the hosted smaller model if latency increases beyond 400ms p95.
devops-bot: INF-4821 status updated: "Edge allowlist and temporary rate bump scheduled" by sam_net. Runbook link: https://redwood.runbooks/infra/INF-4821-step-by-step
sam_net: Provisioning done in staging, will push to prod 08:55 PST and enable at 09:00 PST. Auto-revoke cron added. I'll post the exact ACL change when live.
jin_oncall: I'll run a synthetic load check at 09:10 PST and report latency numbers. Quick pre-check now against staging: `curl -s -w '%{time_total}' -o /dev/null https://api.redwood.test/arborfin/health` => 0.095s.
elaine_cs: Amazing, thank you everyone. I'll update the customer that engineering is handling it and that we have a rollback plan. I'll also add a note to the renewal tracker that we've mitigated the immediate risk and will follow up post-launch. :thumbsup:
sam_net: Live at 09:00 PST. ACL applied, routing weights updated. ACL change: `allow 52.142.18.4/32`, `allow 3.5.6.200/32`. Temporary QPS set to 1200.
jin_oncall: Post-deploy synthetic at 09:12 PST: p95 us-west = 96ms, ap-northeast = 210ms, eu fallback check = 310ms. No errors.
elaine_cs: Closing the loop with the customer now. I'll schedule a post-launch health check in 6 hours and add notes to the renewal doc. Thanks all!
